name: bombadillo
desc: Non-web browser, designed for a growing list of protocols
why: A non-web browser for gopher, gemini and finger; a real door into forgotten internet protocols.

brief.what_it_is: Bombadillo is a non-web browser, a terminal client for browsing internet protocols other than HTTP. Per the Homebrew description it is designed for a growing list of protocols, and the scout notes name gopher, gemini and finger. I could not read its own documentation, so this comes from those two summaries only and I have not verified what it takes in or emits.
brief.why_it_exists: Not verified. The only framing I have is the Homebrew description, 'Non-web browser, designed for a growing list of protocols', and the scout note calling it a door into forgotten internet protocols.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew, which provides a binary named bombadillo. I could not check for any extra setup, runtime, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: Per the scout notes, it covers several small non-web protocols (gopher, gemini, finger) in one client rather than a single-protocol reader. I could not confirm this against the project's own description.
brief.status: unknown. Neither the homepage nor the GitHub repository I guessed could be read, so I have no release date, last commit, or README note.

I also tried https://github.com/makeworld-the-better-one/bombadillo, which returned 404, so that guessed path is probably wrong. Everything above rests on the Homebrew formula description and the scout notes. No README text, commands, quotes, or licence information were available.
